title: Kalman-Filter Adaptive-Beta ETF Pairs + Rolling ADF Cointegration Gate
verdict: NOT CONFIRMED — degenerate cash-parking artifact for 2 of 3 qualified pairs
diagnostic_note: best_oos_sharpe=10.377 (XLF/KBE varA, and LQD/HYG varB) is NOT a real pairs-trading result. Diagnostic check: standalone BIL OOS Sharpe over the same 2018-01-01..2026-06-13 window is 10.385 (ann_ret=0.0252, ann_vol=0.00243) — matches the XLF/KBE headline almost exactly. XLF/KBE never crosses the ENTRY_Z=1.5 Kalman-innovation z-score threshold in 2123 OOS days (max|z|=1.155, frac>1.5=0.0000): the strategy is 100% parked in BIL cash the entire OOS period and is just measuring BIL risk-free Sharpe. LQD/HYG crosses the threshold on only 0.05% of days (max|z|=1.799) — same degeneracy, less extreme. Only GDX/SIL trades meaningfully (frac|z|>1.5=0.0019, max|z|=3.553) and produces a real, non-degenerate OOS Sharpe of 1.259. Root cause hypothesis: the Kalman filter online-adapts both beta and observation-noise variance, which shrinks the innovation z-score scale over time for tightly-cointegrated pairs — the adaptive fix for H307's frozen-beta problem overcorrects and absorbs the tradeable divergence into parameter drift for XLF/KBE and LQD/HYG, leaving GDX/SIL (loosest-fitting pair) as the only one that still generates a genuine signal.
